findings.reason: The protected solution is concise, conventional, and interview-ready. The names pairs_by_distance, worker_index, bike_index, used_bikes, answer, and assigned expose the bucket ordering, tie-break coordinates, availability state, result mapping, and early-stop condition directly. Its compound index names are semantic, and it has no exact generic local named index.

Every worker-bike pair is placed in the bucket for its Manhattan distance. Because workers and bikes are enumerated in ascending index order, insertion order within a bucket is exactly worker index followed by bike index; scanning buckets from distance zero through 1998 therefore visits all pairs in the required global (distance, worker_index, bike_index) order. A pair is accepted exactly when both endpoints remain available. Skipping stale pairs cannot hide a better valid pair, and returning when the assigned count reaches the number of workers yields one distinct bike per worker with the prescribed tie-breaking.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode problem 1057, Python, and the native assignBikes(workers, bikes) interface. Authenticated source evidence confirms n workers and m bikes with 1 <= n <= m <= 1000; exactly two coordinates per row; inclusive coordinate bounds 0 through 999; unique worker and bike locations; Manhattan distance; repeated global selection among available endpoints; worker-index then bike-index tie breaking; and a worker-indexed array of 0-indexed bike indices. The app-local solve adapter preserves that exact contract, and the coordinate bounds make 1998 the maximum distance.

The protected app source and immutable native source bound to verified submission 2067444832 are algorithmically identical: both allocate 1999 distance buckets, enumerate workers before bikes, append the same index pairs, track assigned workers through the answer sentinel, track bikes through a Boolean array, accept the same available pairs, and stop after all workers are assigned. Their only structural differences are the required Solution.assignBikes wrapper and native typing syntax.

The three hidden workloads grow matched worker and bike sets from 8 through 64, an 8x span, while preserving legal unique coordinates and forcing construction and traversal of all W*B pair records. In the final independent run, the exact protected source passed all nine visible correctness cases and all three performance tiers with relative growth exponent +0.00 and a 1.00x largest runtime ratio. An independently correct repeated-search control matched every correctness and benchmark output but failed only the calibrated complexity verdict with exponent +1.91 and a 30.01x largest ratio, cleanly distinguishing O(WB+D) bucket processing from O(W^2B) repeated search.

The Approach accurately derives the bucket order from integer Manhattan distances, explains why nested worker-then-bike insertion implements both tie breakers, proves that stale-pair skipping preserves the greedy rule, and covers equal distances, assigned endpoints, surplus bikes, and the single-worker boundary. Its O(WB+D) time and auxiliary-space claims match the protected implementation and branch manifest.

The modular Reference preserves the X-Y-plane model, repeated global assignment rule, Manhattan-distance formula, worker-before-bike tie breaking, availability semantics, unique-location and size guarantees, worker-indexed return mapping, both explained source examples, all seven constraints, and both hints. Two accessible coordinate tables reproduce every labeled entity, index, and position in the source's two example plots.

A fresh authenticated Premium review verified exactly two explained examples in source order, seven constraints, two hints, two coordinate-plot images, and no tables or follow-up. The modular files are hash-bound in source_fidelity.json to source content hash ace3193df0e7cb53411f2a43d9409d6a54b4a15b4859bd92e72e3646ca2a4831, and the direct fidelity validator returns verified with no errors.

coverage: The authenticated Premium statement contains exactly two examples. Their exact workers, bikes, and output literals appear first in source order, including the uniquely closest first assignment and the worker-index tie that determines the remaining allocation.

All nine ordinary correctness cases are visible samples or trials. They cover the minimum one-worker/one-bike shape, equal and surplus bike counts, both coordinate endpoints 0 and 999, the maximum Manhattan distance 1998, and legal two-coordinate rows with distinct locations.

Material behavior includes a unique closest pair, a bike-index tie, a worker-index tie, a simultaneous two-level tie, a four-way corner tie, stale pairs after earlier assignments, a later choice changed by availability, worker-indexed output order, and unused surplus bikes.

An independent oracle explicitly sorts every legal pair by (Manhattan distance, worker index, bike index), greedily accepts only pairs whose endpoints remain available, and recomputed every authored expected result without using distance buckets.

The oracle, protected app source, and immutable native Solution agreed on all 12 authored correctness-plus-benchmark inputs, 2310 exhaustive legal layouts using one through three workers and bikes on six distinct locations, and 5000 deterministic random legal layouts using up to eight workers and ten bikes.

The 8-, 24-, and 64-worker workloads remain hidden and performance-only, use size consistently as both W and B, span 8x, preserve source legality, and exercise all W*B pair records. A correct O(W^2B) repeated-search control passed every output and failed only scaling against the O(WB+D) protected solution.
